examples.description: Deploy a daily 09:00 operator that drafts overdue-invoice reminders for approval

failure_modes.recovery: Fix the listed issues. Node types: entity_action, http, ai, condition, switch, delay, schedule, approval, prepare_output, manual_trigger, webhook_trigger, schedule_trigger. Edges are { from, to }. Message-shaped steps must be prepare_output nodes.
failure_modes.when: definition_json is not valid vocabulary JSON (unknown/comms node type, cycle, bad edge shape, missing schedule for a schedule trigger)

failure_modes.recovery: Remove the {{credential:...}} reference, or ask an owner or admin to save this workflow.
failure_modes.when: definition_json uses a saved credential ({{credential:...}}) and the caller's role is below admin (reason SIMPLER_WORKFLOW_CREDENTIAL_SAVE_NEEDS_ADMIN)

preconditions: definition_json is a JSON string: { nodes, edges, schedule? }. trigger_type 'schedule' requires definition.schedule.
is_active defaults to 0 (draft) — deploying is an explicit choice, never automatic.

description: Create a workflow — an AI operator's job: validates definition_json (a { nodes, edges, schedule? } graph) against the platform's node vocabulary, refusing unknown node types and any comms/message-shaped step that isn't a prepare_output node, since the platform prepares outputs but never sends them. trigger_type 'schedule' requires a schedule block; next_run_at is then computed server-side from it, never from a caller value. is_active defaults to 0 (draft) — going live is a separate explicit choice. NEXT: workflow_update to fix a rejected definition or flip is_active.
name: workflow_create
